title: exhaust_reference_call documents a correction_cycles>=1 gate that its WHERE clause does not contain
evidence:
+-- failure sites (email bounce / SMS failure webhooks, wrong-person route)
+-- when the row already ran its correction (correction_cycles >= 1): instead
+-- Guarded single-UPDATE (AD-14): only live pre-correction states
+-- (queued / contact_initiated — the states the sweep sends from) plus the
+-- caller's correction_cycles gate; a 0-row result means someone else
+-- transitioned first and the writer stands down.
WHERE id = $1
  AND status IN ('queued', 'contact_initiated')
RETURNING id::text;
detail: The documented firing condition (correction_cycles >= 1) exists only in the header and as a caller obligation — the SQL itself fires on any never-corrected live row. The suite calls rc_sql.exhaust_reference_call directly, so a first-failure row can be terminalized and then stamped, the fabricated signal the header calls impossible.
recommended_fix: Add AND correction_cycles >= 1 to the WHERE so the one-cycle rule lives in the SQL, or reword the header to state the SQL is deliberately unguarded.

title: W3 gate compares mismatched timestamp formats — a same-day stale bounce can compare as post-correction and falsely exhaust
evidence:
+       COALESCE((
+         SELECT e->>'at'
+         FROM jsonb_array_elements(rc.attempts) AS e
+         WHERE e->>'detail' = $4 AND e->>'outcome' = 'delivered'
+         ORDER BY e->>'at' DESC
+         LIMIT 1
+       ), '') AS matched_send_at,
+       -- r1 W3: the correction instant ('' for never-corrected rows).
+       COALESCE(rc.corrected_at::text, '') AS corrected_at,
+       SET attempts = attempts || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('at', to_char(now(), 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'), 'channel', 'email', 'outcome', 'delivered', 'detail', 'new_send_1')),
detail: matched_send_at is 'T'/'Z' ISO text from attempts; corrected_at is timestamptz::text (space separator, session-timezone offset). Lexically 'T' (0x54) > ' ' (0x20), so any same-day send sorts after the correction instant — a pre-correction redelivery compares as post-correction and falsely exhausts + stamps. Tests span different days only, so they cannot catch it.
recommended_fix: Emit corrected_at via the same to_char('YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"') format (or compare parsed timestamps), and add a same-day stale-bounce test.

title: correct on a taken-over row re-queues into a state the sweep permanently ignores
evidence:
+    attempt_count = 0,
+    form_token = NULL,
+    form_token_expires_at = NULL,
+    next_attempt_at = now(),
+    updated_at = now()
+WHERE id = $1
+  AND application_id = $2
+  AND status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status
RETURNING id::text;
+  -- r1 (N12): a take-over landing between the due-SELECT and the send must
+  -- not be followed by a T0 invite — the landlord is handling it (A7).
+  AND taken_over_at IS NULL
detail: correct clears form_token and re-arms the clock but never clears taken_over_at; the T0 claim (and advance, due-SELECT) all guard taken_over_at IS NULL. The B1-promised fresh invite can never fire for a taken-over row — only manual record can advance it, and the corrected contact is never re-invited.
recommended_fix: Clear taken_over_at in correct_reference_call (or the handler) when re-queueing, or explicitly reject correct on taken-over rows.

title: Correction clears the token but not form_opened_at/draft_answers — the prior referee's form state survives into the re-invite
evidence:
+    attempt_count = 0,
+    form_token = NULL,
+    form_token_expires_at = NULL,
        rc.form_token,
        COALESCE(rc.form_opened_at::text, '') AS form_opened_at,
        COALESCE(rc.draft_answers::text, '')  AS draft_answers,
detail: sweep_due (the re-invite read) selects form_opened_at and draft_answers; a wrong-person row corrected via B1 keeps both. The fresh invite carries the previous referee's opened-at and draft answers instead of a clean form state.
recommended_fix: Also NULL form_opened_at and draft_answers in correct_reference_call so the corrected referee's re-invite starts with clean state.

title: New payload negative control is vacuous — the sentinel string appears nowhere in the diff
evidence:
+  // RC4.3 note: the referee's CONTACT snapshot now legitimately rides the
+  // payload (the §7.7 take-over chips + §8.3 edit prefill need it) — the
+  // negative control moved to a still-internal marker (form_token is never
+  // selected by the detail read).
+  string.contains(body, "form_token_internal_sentinel") |> should.be_false
detail: Unless a fixture outside this diff seeds a form_token with exactly 'form_token_internal_sentinel', the assertion cannot fail — a real form_token leak carrying any other value passes. The replaced control (a real seeded email absent from the body) actually bit.
recommended_fix: Seed the fixture row's form_token with the sentinel value before fetching so the absence assertion has teeth.

title: Substitute's 'existing' successor can be a skipped/awaiting_correction row — 200 with no queued successor
evidence:
+  ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (
+    'form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused', 'objected',
+    'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed', 'partial'
+  )
+  DO NOTHING
+  AND rc.status NOT IN (
+    'form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused', 'objected',
+    'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed', 'partial'
+  )
detail: The live-slot predicates exclude only the listed terminals; 'skipped' and 'awaiting_correction' rows both conflict and qualify as 'existing'. Substituting a terminal row when such a row occupies the slot returns a 200 no-op — the landlord's new referee is never queued or invited.
recommended_fix: Restrict the conflict/existing predicates (and the matching partial index) to invite-able states such as queued/contact_initiated, or 409 when the occupant is not invite-able.
